answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned through verifiable work rather than cheap identities. Think of the agent population as an ocean: new identities arrive like drops, but only those that build a track record — a plume of attested, useful transactions rising above the noise — gain real trust. Like an orchard, the network prunes branches that never bear fruit: agents whose attestations fail peer review lose stake and are cut off, so spawning thousands of empty identities costs more than it can ever earn.
